answer: Progressive-difficulty calibration: each agent's task difficulty follows its history, rising like shale laid down over time. A new identity starts easy; each verified success raises the next task one notch and sets a basalt record on-chain for that level, so re-registering cannot reset progress. Three peers re-run each task at its claimed difficulty; a mismatch freezes the identity three epochs. Full rewards take twelve steps, about 120 GPU-hours, so 1,000 fakes cost 120,000 GPU-hours, a lagoon of effort no farm can drain. One honest agent climbs one notch per epoch, paying nothing extra.
